body.x: OTITON Medical (CEO Kim Jaeyoung) participated in CES Unveiled on January 5 (local time), a pre-event to the official opening of CES 2025. Founded in 2022, OTITON Medical specializes in developing user-friendly and effective healthcare solutions for individuals and families. The company aims to revolutionize global healthcare with advanced medical devices like its Doctor in Home smart platform.

The Doctor in Home platform, previously recognized with a CES 2025 Innovation Award, was showcased again at CES Unveiled. The solution drew significant attention for its innovative approach to enabling home-based health monitoring through cutting-edge IoT (Internet of Things) and AI (Artificial Intelligence) technologies.

The platform includes advanced digital healthcare devices, such as a smart thermometer incorporating a precision temperature sensor and an otoscope camera for middle ear diagnosis. These devices allow users to gather diagnostic data at home and transfer it to a connected smartphone app to monitor conditions like ear infections or track recovery progress.

body.cap: OTITON Medical introduced its Doctor in Home platform to AVING News reporter Alex Sigrist during CES Unveiled. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The Doctor in Home platform is designed to extend accessibility in countries permitting telemedicine. It enables medical professionals to utilize data collected via the smart thermometer, enhancing healthcare delivery for patients in remote or underserved areas.

The platform also supports multi-user data management, making it ideal for families to monitor the health of all members periodically or in real time. Its user-friendly interface and ergonomic hardware design make it accessible to individuals of all ages, from children to older people.

An OTITON Medical representative explained, “Our devices use precision sensors and AI technology to enable real-time health data monitoring and analysis, ensuring effective and systematic health management. We aim to increase brand recognition and showcase the platform’s innovative features at CES 2025.”

The representative added, “Through global promotional efforts, we hope to connect with potential customers and partners, paving the way for new business opportunities and market entry. We’re particularly focusing on high-demand markets like Japan, Australia, and the US, where advanced medical technologies and digital healthcare solutions are in high demand.”

body.cap: OTITON Medical presented its Doctor in Home platform to international media representatives at CES Unveiled. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: OTITON Medical participated in CES 2025 as part of the Seoul Pavilion in Eureka Park, the startup-focused exhibition area. The Seoul Pavilion, expanded by over 50% from the previous year to 1,040 square meters, featured 104 startups. It represents a collaboration between three Seoul districts (Gangnam, Geumcheon, and Gwanak), five startup support organizations (SBA, Seoul Tourism Organization, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul AI Hub, and Campus Town Growth Center), and eight universities (Konkuk, Kyung Hee, Kookmin, Dongguk, Sogang, Seoul National University of Science and Technology, Yonsei, and Chung-Ang).
AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
